result.title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
result.summary: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Map2Vid 任务，把具身导航视频生成改写为 BEV 地图到视频的合成问题，并构建含 10 万余条导航序列、61 个室内场景的数据集，以及整合多控制信号的统一框架和逐步弱化非地图输入的课程训练策略。
AI.relevance_reason: BEV 地图作为显式承载全局布局与路线的空间条件，可能为 LVR 中几何与任务必要信息的表示方式提供参照；其「逐步弱化非地图输入」的课程训练或可类比辅助条件移除与贡献分配，属待核查线索而非已验证结论。
